as_told.title: Lost time from 2 a.m. to dawn; friend declines regression hypnosis

plain: A guard at Vandenberg Air Force Base in California, Richard Barth, says that in 1964 the whole memory of a strange night came flooding back to him about two weeks after it happened. He tells Michels he lay paralyzed, then woke and "got flooded with this whole experience," and was sure "it wasn't a dream." He describes lost time, a gap in his memory that he puts from about 2 a.m. until dawn, and asks what went on in it. In another part of the conversation he adds that about 20 years later a friend turned down regression hypnosis, a kind of hypnosis meant to bring back buried memories, and he names a man called Lonnie and Robert Hastings in connection with the account. If his memory is right, something happened to a guard of nuclear missiles that he was not meant to remember.
